Report DescriptionON MARCH 27, SECTOR NEW ORLEANS INITIATED A CIC CALL TO REPORT THAT THE M/V SIROCCO (FLAG: PANAMA) HAD ALLIDED WITH THE UNCLE SAM MOSAIC FERTILIZER FACILITY. AT 0230 ON MARCH 27, SECTOR NEW ORLEANS RECEIVED A REPORT THAT THE M/V SIROCCO HAD BROKE FREE FROM ITS MOORINGS IN CONVENT MARINE TERMINAL IN CONVENT, LA AT MILE MARKED 160.9 ON THE LOWER MISSISSIPPI RIVER. ASSIST TUGS WERE ABLE TO RECOVER THE VESSEL AND MANEUVER IT TO THE UPPER GRANDVIEW ANCHORAGE AT MILE MARKER 147 WHERE THE VESSEL WAS SAFELY ANCHORED. AT 0430 CDT SECTOR NEW ORLEANS RECEIVED A REPORT THAT WHEN THE M/V SIROCCO BROKE FREE IT HAD STRUCK THE UNCLE SAM MOSAIC FERTILIZER FACILITY AND HAD CAUSED SIGNIFICANT DAMAGE. THE FACILITY SUSTAINED DAMAGE TO ITS PIER AND TWO BARGES MOORED THERE. THE FACILITY REPORTED THAT THE DAMAGE IS ESTIMATED AT ONE MILLION DOLLARS MAKING THIS A MAJOR MARINE CASUALTY. M/V SIROCCO SUSTAINED DAMAGE TO THEIR ACCOMMODATION LADDER AND SCUFFED PAINT. NO POLLUTION OR INJURIES WERE REPORTED. NTSB HAS BEEN INCLUDED ON THIS EMAIL. THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN.

THE CALLER REPORTED THAT A VESSEL RAN AGROUND OFF A PRIVATE PRIVATE PROPERTY AT OR NEAR THE OLD BRIDGE ROAD ON UNKNOWN DATE. THE USCG FOUND THE VESSEL DURING A PATROL ON APR. 07, 2017. ACCORDING TO THE STATEMENT MADE BY OWNER OF THE PROPERTY, THE OWNER OF THE VESSEL LEFT THE VESSEL AT THE LOCATION AGAINST THE WILL OF THE PROPERTY OWNER. AS OF DATE OF THIS REPORTING (MAY 23, 2017), THE VESSEL IS STILL GROUNDED AT THE SAME LOCATION. THE OWNER OF THE BOAT IS YET HAVE A FINAL PLAN TO HOW AND WHEN THE VESSEL WILL BE TOWED AWAY.
